1a.note: DISAGREE on the transcription note and rubric; verdict (false) and steps agree. (1) The note offers frequencies 1,1,1,3 -> 2,2,2,4 as an example where the structure changes: with arbitrary tie-breaks (GATE1 ruling) 2,2,2,4 can still produce all three tree shapes of 1,1,1,3 (plus the balanced one), so it does not show the tree changes. The steps use 1,1,2,3 vs 3,3,4,5, which is clean (unique shape each: depths (3,3,2,1) vs (2,2,2,2)) and is the right example. (2) The official counterexample (2,2|5 vs 7|4,4) is valid under the course convention used in Q1b/Q1c that the lighter sibling goes left (the code of b flips from 1 to 0), yet rubric point 4 and pitfall 1 present it as invalid. Reword: the official example is acceptable on the left<=right convention; the stronger example is 1,1,2,3 vs 3,3,4,5.
